text:
nina.support: FYI customer 'LexaHealth' just escalated — they see p99 TTFB on streaming endpoints jump from ~120ms to ~1.6s starting ~02:10 UTC. non-stream (sync) endpoints p99 stayed ~200ms.
ethan.infra: timeline? did anything roll at 02:10?
nina.support: customer first noticed at 02:12, we see a small surge in streaming error/latency alerts across region-eq1 starting 02:08. No deploys in that window per deploy-bot.
maya.runtime: I'm seeing an increase in first-chunk delay on stream paths for some sessions. p50 first-chunk 110ms, p99 first-chunk 1.6s. total generation time unchanged.
sam.network: could be head-of-line due to HTTP/2 stream multiplexing or proxy coalescing heuristics. Any pattern on connection reuse?
ethan.infra: pulling traces for a few requests from the customer now. Repro token: 9a3f..
ethan.infra: trace snippet: 
```
START -> ingress-proxy (accept) 0.8ms -> conn-mux 0.9ms -> runtime-coalesce WAIT 1.2s -> runtime-flush -> model-step 40ms -> outbound 2.1ms
```
nina.support: customer provided curl for streaming: 
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate" -d '{"prompt":"...","stream":true}'
```
sam.network: that WAIT line fits conn-level coalescing. We've got heuristics: hold small writes up to 8KB or 50ms before flushing to avoid tiny frames. If model emits very small first chunks but then stalls due to batching, that combo -> big TTFB.
maya.runtime: right — we recently tightened coalesce window for CPU hosts to improve throughput under load. Looks like it inadvertently affected customers with many short responses.
ethan.infra: can you reproduce locally with a synthetic that emits a tiny first chunk then pauses? I'll try a toy server: 
```
# python pseudo
write(sock, "data: a")
sleep(1.2)
write(sock, "data: rest")
```
ethan.infra: reproduction on staging with same coalesce settings: streaming first chunk delayed ~1.2s, sync/gathered response returned as single payload immediately ~140ms.
nina.support: customer says switching to non-streaming endpoint mitigates for them but they need streaming semantics for progressive UX.
maya.runtime: mitigation ideas: 
- lower first-chunk coalesce timeout for streaming routes (eg 50ms -> 15ms)
- special-case immediate-first-chunk flush: if model has output bytes >0, always flush first chunk immediately
- heuristics by client: user-agent hint to prefer low-latency flush
- fallback: detect >500ms TTFB and auto-fallback to non-stream for that connection (bad for progressive UI)
sam.network: also check proxy-level Nagle-like buffering (h2 windowing) — older proxy version had a bug that coalesced across streams when connection had many half-open streams. Not sure it's enabled in our fleet though.
ethan.infra: log snippet from one impacted request (ingress-proxy): 
```
INGRESS: conn_id=xyz streams_active=12 bytes_buffered=4KB coalesce_timer=50ms
RUNTIME: route=stream host=cpu-6 coalesce_window=50ms first_chunk_bytes=5
```
maya.runtime: quick patch candidate: immediate-first-chunk flush + emit metric `stream.first_chunk_flushed_immediate` and roll as a 10% canary. If it reduces p99 we can widen.
ethan.infra: agree. Let's also add a short-term rollback knob in config to revert tighter coalesce if regressions elsewhere.
nina.support: I'll tell customer we have a canary/patrol plan and ask for a short time window for testing.
sam.network: I'll grep proxy config across region-eq1 to confirm no recent change to mux buffering.
ethan.infra: assigning tasks: maya -> quick patch + canary (PR), sam -> verify proxy config and confirm no global change, me -> set up traces + create dashboard for stream.first_chunk_ttfb p50/p95/p99, nina -> customer comms and collect a few more example request IDs.
maya.runtime: will open PR in ~30m, mark canary 10% region-eq1. Patch will: 
1) flush first non-empty chunk immediately (unbuffered write)
2) metric emit

PR note: keep old coalesce config as fallback (env var STREAM_FLUSH_MODE=legacy|immediate).
deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: maya.runtime/stream-flush-imm -> canary(10%) at 1745201800; status: pending.
ethan.infra: monitoring: created dashboard panel and alert: if stream.first_chunk_p99 > 400ms escalate.
nina.support: sent message to LexaHealth: we're running a canary that should reduce first-chunk latency for your traffic and will monitor for 30m, will follow up with results.
devops-bot: canary deploy completed at 1745201825 -> 10% region-eq1.
maya.runtime: canary telemetry: initial 10k requests: first_chunk_p99 dropped from 1.6s -> 120ms for canary nodes. No error increase.
sam.network: proxy checks clean, no global config drift. Looks localized to runtime coalescing change.
ethan.infra: widening to 40% for 15m to get better sample.
nina.support: customer confirms improved experience in test after ~5m. "Huge improvement, thanks"
maya.runtime: rolling to 100% in 10m if no regressions. Posting rollback plan in PR.
ethan.infra: follow-ups: 
- bake metric into SLO/observability for streaming first-chunk TTFB
- run a perf sweep to check throughput impact of immediate-first-chunk flush under high QPS
- add client-side guidance in docs for when to prefer non-streaming vs streaming for tiny responses
nina.support: closing loop with customer after full rollout and offering help to switch back if they prefer non-streaming.
ethan.infra: thanks team. Will keep thread open for perf sweep results and any edge regressions.
